key_insight: MECx uses a bond-informed surrogate energy model to find low-energy ordered configurations in multi-principal element alloys more efficiently than direct DFT-based Monte Carlo.
engineering_relevance: Identifying alloy ordering can help engineers investigate local structures that influence mechanical and thermodynamic properties.
method: Select training configurations stratified in bond-count space.
Train surrogate energy models on 100 DFT-labeled configurations per alloy.
Guide Monte Carlo searches and examine ordering, temperature response, and simulated neutron diffraction.
evidence_signal: Across ternary, quaternary, and quinary BCC alloys, MECx found lower-energy candidates than direct DFT-based Monte Carlo within practical computational limits, with transfer demonstrated to selected binary subsystems without retraining.
watch_item: Transferability was demonstrated only for selected binary subsystems; broader alloy chemistries and crystal structures require validation.
paper_title: Bond-informed search for ordered configurations in multi-principal element alloys
